samples.text:
The maps shows the grounds of a city hospital in 2005 and in the present time. Overall, the hospital has more buildings and car parks now, and the empty land was used for new facilities.

In 2005, the main hospital building was in the centre and a road connected it with Hill Road in the south. There was one car park for staff and visitors in the south-west, a big garden in the east, nurses' housing in the north and a clinic in the north-west. The north-east was vacant land.

Nowadays, the main building and the road is the same. The car park has been divided in two part, a visitor car park and a staff car park above it. A children's hospital was built in the south part of the garden, so the garden is smaller. The nurses' housing has been replaced by a cancer treatment centre and the clinic become a health centre. Also, a multi-storey car park and a helipad have been built on the vacant land.
samples.why: Overview present but general · main changes reported in a simple sequence · limited linking (Also, so) · adequate vocabulary · errors in agreement, tense, plurals and prepositions that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The two maps illustrate how the grounds of a city hospital have changed since 2005. Overall, the site has been developed considerably, with several new medical buildings and extra parking, while the main hospital building and the access road from Hill Road in the south remain unchanged.

The most noticeable development has occurred in the north of the site. The vacant land in the north-east has been used for a multi-storey car park and a helipad, and the nurses' housing to the north of the main building has been replaced by a larger cancer treatment centre. Similarly, the clinic in the north-west has made way for a larger health centre.

In the southern half of the grounds, the single car park for staff and visitors has been divided into two, with a visitor car park in the south-west and a staff car park directly to its north. To the east, the garden has lost its southern section to a new children's hospital, so it is now less than half its former size. Finally, a short road has been added, leading from the eastern side of the main building towards the garden.
samples.why: Clear overview · changes logically grouped by area · good range of cohesive devices · some less common vocabulary (made way, divided into) · generally accurate structures with only occasional minor imprecision.

samples.text:
The maps compare the grounds of a city hospital in 2005 and today. In short, the site has become far more intensively used, as open space has been built on to provide additional medical services and parking, although the central hospital building and its access road from Hill Road are unchanged.

The northern part of the site has undergone the most extensive change. What was once vacant land in the north-east is now occupied by a multi-storey car park and, further east, a helipad. Next to them, the nurses' housing has been replaced by a somewhat larger cancer treatment centre, while the clinic in the north-west has given way to a health centre.

Further south, parking arrangements have been reorganised: the single staff and visitor car park in the south-west has been split, with visitors now using the southern section and staff the northern one. On the eastern side of the grounds, the garden, which once stretched from near Hill Road as far as the level of the hospital's northern wall, has been reduced to a strip in the north, as a children's hospital now stands on its southern half. A short road connecting the main building with the garden completes the changes.
samples.why: Well-judged overview · changes selected and located with precision · cohesion managed naturally across paragraphs · wide, accurate vocabulary (intensively used, reorganised) · complex structures used flexibly and without error.
